title: Clinicopathological Characteristics of Early-Onset Versus Later-Onset Rectal Cancer: An 11-Year Single Centre Retrospective Study from Craiova, Romania
content: Background: Rectal cancer is increasingly diagnosed in younger adults, but data from Eastern Europe are limited. We compared rectal cancer in patients aged ≤50 years with that in older patients at a Romanian tertiary centre. Methods: We retrospectively reviewed 4171 patients with rectal cancer admitted to the County Emergency Clinical Hospital of Craiova between 2015 and 2025. Patients aged ≤50 years (n = 144) were compared with patients aged ≥51 years (n = 3870 analysed) for sex, residence, tumour location and histological type; stage and treatment were described in the younger group; resection margins and 3-year survival were also analysed. Results: Younger patients (mean age 44.6 ± 5.7 years) did not differ from older patients in sex (59.4% vs. 61.2% male; p = 0.67) or rural residence (65.6% vs. 70.9%; p = 0.19). Recto-sigmoid tumours were half as frequent (20.8% vs. 40.7%; p < 0.001) and mucinous adenocarcinoma was less frequent (2.4% vs. 16.6%; p < 0.001). Among younger patients, 58.3% of staged tumours were pT3–pT4 and 26.0% had metastases at diagnosis. Diversion procedures increased from 0% at T1 to 53.6% at T4 (p < 0.001). Molecular testing was documented in 11 patients. Among 113 resected patients (margin status recorded in 108), 94.4% had negative margins; 3-year survival (Kaplan–Meier) was 80.6% after R0 and 33.3% after R1 resection, and 20.2% in 26 patients without resection (supratumoral stoma) (log-rank p < 0.001). Conclusions: Rectal cancer in patients aged ≤50 years differed from later-onset disease mainly in anatomical distribution and was frequently advanced at diagnosis. Prospective multicentre studies with molecular profiling are needed.
